why: D2's implicit-main fallback: two scripts with no `package` statement at all, both declaring `usage` — proving the ids stay distinct and path-keyed (`perl:scripts/a.pl.usage` vs `perl:scripts/b.pl.usage`) rather than colliding the way a single shared `main` Type would. `require "common.pl";` (a bare filename, not the full `lib/common.pl` path) exercises `import_link.py`'s C-style path-suffix matcher, the D7 case a namespace-keyed `use` target never needs. Named `scripts/`, not `bin/`: when this case was written `bin/` was in `extractor.DEFAULT_IGNORE_DIRS` and every front-end dropped it silently. Since B63 the graph walks a `bin/` unless a .NET project or solution sits beside it (`walk_rules.is_dotnet_output_dir`), and since SSPN-333 every repository walker applies the same rule through `walk_rules.walk_repo`; the case keeps `scripts/` so its ids stay stable.
